help.gettingStartedIntro: Follow these steps to set up your AI research lab and start building assistants.

configure.title: Configure AI Provider
configure.desc: Add an AI provider to power the builder and experiments.
configure.details: Go to Settings, click 'Add Provider', fill in the name, model, API key, and endpoint URL. Click 'Test connection' to verify, then 'Set active' to enable it.

build.title: Build Your First Assistant
build.desc: Use the AUTOMAT(E) framework to create a structured system prompt.
build.details: Open Assistant Builder, fill in the 8 AUTOMAT(E) fields across 4 tabs (Identity, Action, Style, Safety). Click 'Generate System Prompt' to create the prompt, then 'Save Assistant' to store it.

experiment.title: Run Your First Experiment
experiment.desc: Test AI behavior across different categories.
experiment.details: Open Research Lab, click 'New Experiment', enter a title and select a category (Truthfulness, Sycophancy, Bias, etc.). Click 'Run Experiment' to execute and view results.

security.title: Test Security
security.desc: Check your assistant's resistance to prompt injection attacks.
security.details: Open Security, click 'Run Tests'. The system will run 9 tests across 4 suites (Direct Injection, Indirect Injection, Scope Violation, Data Exposure) against your active AI provider.

faqList.q1: Why do I need to configure a provider first?
faqList.a1: The AI provider (OpenAI, DeepSeek, etc.) powers the Generate, Experiment, and Security features. Without an active provider, the Assistant Builder will only show a local template without AI generation.
faqList.a2: AUTOMAT(E) is a structured framework for building system prompts. It stands for Act As, User & Audience, Targeted Action, Output Definition, Mode/Tone, Atypical Cases, Topic Whitelisting, and Examples. It ensures your prompts are complete and well-structured.
faqList.q3: How does the security test work?
faqList.a3: The security test sends attack prompts to your active AI provider and evaluates the responses. It tests 9 attack vectors across 4 categories: Direct Injection, Indirect Injection, Scope Violation, and Data Exposure. Results show BLOCKED (pass) or EXPOSED (fail).
faqList.q4: Can I use multiple AI providers?
faqList.a4: Yes! You can add multiple providers in Settings. However, only one provider can be 'active' at a time. The active provider is used for all AI operations (Generate, Experiments, Security tests).
faqList.q5: What happens if no provider is active?
faqList.a5: The Assistant Builder will fall back to a local template (no AI generation). Experiments and Security tests will fail with an error message. Always ensure at least one provider is active.
faqList.q6: How do I export/import my data?
faqList.a6: Go to Settings and use the 'Export JSON' button to download all providers. Use 'Import JSON' to upload a providers.json file. Library items can be downloaded individually as JSON files.

welcome.title: Welcome to AI Prompt Research Lab
welcome.desc: A platform for building, testing, and securing AI assistants using the AUTOMAT(E) framework. Let's walk through the essential steps to get you started.

provider.title: Step 1: Configure a Provider
provider.desc: Add an AI provider (OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama, etc.) in Settings. This powers the Generate, Experiment, and Security features. Without it, the builder only shows local templates.

builder.title: Step 2: Build Your Assistant
builder.desc: Use the AUTOMAT(E) Builder to create structured system prompts. Fill in 8 fields across 4 tabs, generate the prompt, preview it, and save your assistant.

experiment.title: Step 3: Experiment & Secure
experiment.desc: Run behavior experiments in Research Lab and test prompt injection resistance in Security. Compare results across models and categories.
